plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and prized for ornamental use and for its fruit, used in pickles and liqueurs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are traditionally celebrated as a harbinger of spring in East Asia, and they often bloom while snow is still on the ground.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler petals and blue-green strap-like leaves. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring and is the ancestor of many garden daffodils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (March to April in Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids, and one of them, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree or large shrub with feathery foliage that bears fluffy, fragrant golden flower balls. It is Australia's national floral emblem and an important food source for native insects and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July to October), with some blooming into early autumn in cooler zones and varied wattles flowering in March
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the green and gold of the wattle inspired the colors of the national sporting teams.

plants.name: Eranthis hyemalis
plants.description: A low-growing tuberous perennial with bright buttercup-like flowers sitting on a ruff of green leaf-like bracts. It pushes through frozen soil and snow to flower in woodlands and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Southern Europe, from France to the Balkans; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Winter aconite flowers close up in cold or cloudy weather and open only in sunshine, which protects their pollen from damp conditions.
